subject: MedNexus pilot: short-retention & PII carveout — next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@mednexus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: MedNexus pilot: short-retention & PII carveout — recap and proposed next steps

Hi Laura / Derek — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of customer's ask
- MedNexus wants a pilot configuration where any user-submitted PII is not persisted beyond request processing (effectively 0-retention for sensitive fields) while non-PII operational telemetry is retained for 7 days for debugging.
- They also require a contractual carveout documenting the short-retention behavior, evidence that KV/prefix caches are cleared, and a mechanism for Redaction/Deletion on demand.

2) Redwood's proposed approach (pilot scope)
- Create a dedicated short-ttl model route with ephemeral logging enabled: PII fields are redacted at ingress via customer-specified patterns; logs containing redacted tokens are retained for 0 days (no disk storage) and token-level telemetry is sent to a short-term buffer (7d) for troubleshooting only.
- Deploy the pilot on a single dedicated pool in us-west with strict network isolation and KMS-managed keys.

3) Action items / timeline
- Laura: send the final list of PII field names and a copy of the Security Questionnaire we should mark as high priority (you mentioned a compliance packet).
- Derek: confirm whether MedNexus wants on-call windows for the pilot (SOC contact) and whether legal needs the proposed clause before we spin up infra.
- Redwood (Marissa): share a draft retention clause and a short configuration spec by Tue 2/16.
- Redwood (Irene): schedule a follow-up call with Legal & Security if you confirm the list; propose Wed 2/17 or Thu 2/18.

Attachments: I attached the proposed-retention-clause.docx with a suggested 0-day store for redacted logs and a 7-day operational buffer for anonymized telemetry. Also attaching our standard security playbook for ephemeral routes.

If this matches your understanding, I suggest we align on the PII list today so Marissa and Karthik can start drafting the clause and run it through legal.

Thanks —
Irene

Thanks Irene — that captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- PII list: we will send a table of ~12 fields by EOD today (names, emails, SSN-like IDs, insurance ids). These must be treated as sensitive; we expect redaction at ingress and zero persistence.
- Audit evidence: we need a short runbook describing where data flows and an affirmation that KV cache entries containing sensitive tokens will be purged immediately after response. Is that something you can include in the clause or as a separate addendum?
- Legal: we do want to review the clause before the pilot spins up. We can provide comments in DocuSign or marked-up Word — whichever is easier.

Two asks: 
1) Please mark the proposed-retention-clause.docx as "for legal review" and indicate which sections are negotiable vs. hard requirements.
2) Share an internal contact for your security engineer who can do a 30-min freeze-frame walkthrough of the pipeline for our security ops.

We'll aim to have internal sign-off on the PII list by Tue morning and can do the follow-up call Wed morning PT.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MedNexus pilot: short-retention & PII carveout — draft clause and evidence pack

Hi Laura — looping in Karthik (Privacy & Compliance) to provide the evidence language and to outline the negotiable items. Draft summary below and attached is a marked-up clause.

Draft summary (high level)
- "0-retention" for PII: Redwood will not persist redacted PII to disk or long-term object storage. Any tokens flagged as PII are removed from persistent logs and are not written to S3/backing stores. This is non-negotiable for fields the customer designates as PII in the pilot scope.
- Operational telemetry: anonymized telemetry (no PII tokens) retained up to 7 days in a short-term buffer accessible only to Redwood incident responders. This buffer is encrypted and access-controlled.
- KV cache purge: KV/prefix caches where PII tokens could be present will be flushed after request completion; we will provide a purge confirmation event in the audit trail.
- Evidence pack: we will provide (a) a short architecture diagram, (b) a cache purge log sample, (c) a signed statement from our security team outlining encryption/KMS usage.

Negotiable items
- Wording around "purge confirmation" (we can provide a signed event but not a live stream of cache state).
- Whether the anonymized telemetry includes coarse usage counters vs. per-request timing.

Next steps
- I attached the proposed-retention-clause.docx with comments in track changes. If MedNexus can accept the non-negotiable points above, Karthik and I will prepare the evidence pack and coordinate the technical walkthrough (30 min) on Wed 2/17 09:00 PT.

Regards,
